messages:
Maria Lopez: Spinning up a focused benchmark for 'spec-decoder-lite' — goal is a tightly reproducible pipeline to compare speculative decoding vs normal decode on a quantized 13B candidate. Plan: paired generations, seed control, log token-level reuse, and track both latency and small-scope quality (chrF + Kendall on ranked outputs).

Kevin Tran: Sounds good. Quick ask: define 'small-scope quality' concretely in the runbook so CI can gate. Also we should pick a deterministic predictor config or document nondeterminism impact.

Maria Lopez: Agreed. Runbook notes: small-scope quality = (1) chrF on curated holdout_2k, (2) per-example chrF delta + Kendall tau of n-best ranking between baseline and spec. Gate thresholds: chrF drop >1.0% overall or any example with >5 point drop triggers triage.

Sasha Iyer: Important: predictor nondet if temp>0. We'll freeze predictor to temp=0 (greedy) for the primary run. If we test stochastic predictor later, we'll separate as an experiment. Paired seed generation requires predictor determinism.

Devin Park: Proposed primary config: predictor=greedy (temp=0), spec-steps=2, generator temp=0.7 top_p=0.92. Quant: q4f16 for full model. Batch size: 1 for latency runs, batch=8 for throughput sweep. Repeat=250 for stability.

ops-bot: bench triggered by @Maria Lopez. Job id: sd-lite-202504-11. Started 1746012300.

QA Sam: Dataset plan: holdout_2k + stress_short_200. We'll compute per-example chrF and also a quick hallucination heuristic (named SROUGE-lite) to surface big content drops.

Kevin Tran: Need to capture fallback metrics: fallback_count, tokens_wasted, median_extra_tokens_when_fallback. Also track percent requests with fallback and distribution of fallback positions (early/late).

Maria Lopez: Yes — logging schema: total_tokens, reused_tokens, fallback_count, extra_tokens_mean, kv_cache_hit_rate, p95_latency_warm, p95_latency_cold. We'll tag each request with predictor_config and quant_profile.

Devin Park: Local command to reproduce (put into CI):

```bash
bench run \
  --job spec-decoder-lite \
  --model redwood-llamax-13b \
  --quant q4f16 \
  --decoding speculative \
  --spec-predictor greedy \
  --spec-steps 2 \
  --generator-temp 0.7 \
  --top-p 0.92 \
  --seed 1234 \
  --batch 1 \
  --repeats 250 \
  --dataset holdout_2k \
  --output artifact://sd-lite-202504-11.json
```

ops-bot: bench sd-lite-202504-11 finished. baseline: p95=232ms, median=45ms, tokens=1.00x, chrF(avg)=0.646. speculative: p95=160ms, median=33ms, tokens=1.10x, chrF(avg)=0.641. fallback_count=22/250 (8.8%), extra_tokens_mean=2.9, kv_cache_hit=0.88. Artifacts: s3://bench/sd-lite-202504-11/artifact.json

Sasha Iyer: Latency improvement looks solid. chrF drop -0.005 (~0.8%) so under the 1% gate but not negligible. We should inspect per-example where chrF loss >4 points; do we have category tags on prompts (code/doc/math)?

QA Sam: I'll generate per-example CSV and attach categorized tags. If we see clusters (e.g., multi-step reasoning) we can open triage. Uploading now.

Kevin Tran: Also computed Kendall tau between baseline and spec n-best ranks: tau = 0.976 for top-5, which is reassuring. But some examples show reordering in code completions; will flag those.

Maria Lopez: Action items from this run: (A) QA Sam: attach per-example CSV + flagged categories (EOD), (B) Devin: run predictor=small-7b (same seed) to check cheaper predictor tradeoff, (C) Ops: run batch=8 throughput sweep + flamegraphs, (D) Sasha/Kevin: write short gating doc (thresholds + why). If triage finds >25 examples in a category we pause rollout.

Devin Park: Extra experiment idea: use a q2 predictor-only quant (if supported) and measure predictor latency reduction vs added fallback. Might lower overall cost. Also try spec-steps=3 to see latency/quality knee.

Sasha Iyer: Careful: mixed quant paths can force an expensive dequant fallback. Add 'fallback_path_type' to logs (native/convert) so we can separate pure predictor misses vs dequant overhead.

Maria Lopez: Good call. I'll update the runbook to include log schema and CSV column descriptions. Plan to open a tiny PR with results and artifacts linked. If QA flags systemic regressions we hold.

ops-bot: Reminder: include artifact links in PR description per policy.

Kevin Tran: Ping me once artifacts are linked. I'll run a small script to recompute Kendall and extract top regression examples for the triage doc.

Maria Lopez: Thanks team — will follow up with PR and schedule a 30m sync if we need to deep-dive triage results.
